items.summary: Released November 1: one workspace on your own machine lets Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot and more split a job, each in its own git worktree, messaging each other as they go; when one agent runs out of usage, its task moves to another with a record of what was done, and nothing ships before you review it. Open source (MIT), no account and no model of its own — it drives the tools already signed in on your computer.
items.title: Friday: Run multiple coding agents as a team, locally, with handoffs when one hits its limit

items.summary: Introduced November 2: a self-hosted control plane that turns computers you own into an always-on agent workspace, with built-in networking, a shared remote filesystem usable concurrently without de-sync, and native browser and computer use. It works with any model provider or with an existing Claude Code or ChatGPT Codex subscription, and can run on a single machine. Open source (MIT), chats not shared by default.
items.title: Mainplane: An open-source “agent shed” where agents keep working across your own computers

items.summary: New coverage November 4: an open-source (MIT) Android app with an on-phone runner and Midscene screenshot understanding, operating apps in natural language across apps, with no ADB, Shizuku or root needed for everyday use. A computer-side plugin can also drive a paired phone over a pinned Wi-Fi connection. Inference still goes to a configured vision model; requires an arm64 Android 11+ phone.
items.title: Tapilot: A screenshot agent that runs on your Android phone — no computer required
